c1.note: The March 28, 2025 xAI deal valued X at $33B in equity. This is the last explicit standalone X valuation, but it is superseded by the 2026 SpaceX merger.

c2.note: Reuters and Musk's own post both describe the deal as all-stock.

c3.note: Musk's post says '$33 billion ($45B less $12B debt)'. The $45B figure includes the debt.

c4.note: Sullivan & Cromwell calls $45B the enterprise value and $33B the value after the $12B of debt. The caution is a valid framing.

c5.note: The deal valued xAI at $80B. This is context rather than X's value.

c7.note: Reuters reported the remark, which came from analyst Gil Luria, not from Reuters itself. The $1B-above-2022 point is correct.

c8.note: Musk acquired Twitter for about $44B in 2022. This is historical background.

c10.note: A 79% cut from $44B implies about $9B, not $12.5B ($12.5B would be a cut of roughly 72%). The claim is internally inconsistent.

c11.note: Fidelity estimated the company at $15B at the end of May 2023. This is historical.

c12.note: CNBC reports the merger completed Feb. 2, 2026 and an IPO expected at $1.25T. X now sits inside SpaceX, so there is no standalone valuation.

c13.note: The acquisition valued xAI at $250B and SpaceX at $1T. X is a subsidiary of xAI.

c14.note: CNBC says xAI was valued at about $230B in a $20B round that closed in early 2026.

c15.note: CNBC says SpaceX opened a secondary share sale last year at an $800B valuation.

c16.note: The IPO raised $75B (about $86B with overallotment); the pricing valuation was $1.77T and the first-day market cap about $2.1T, so '$2 trillion' is a loose round-up.

c17.note: SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 per share on June 11, 2026.

c18.note: Trading began June 12 as SPCX; the pricing valuation of $1.77T was the largest IPO ever.

c19.note: The first-day close was $161 (+19%), for a market cap of about $2.1T.

c21.note: Yahoo shows a 52-week low of 104.83 and a previous close of 143.09.

c22.note: Wikipedia gives a $211 peak and $123-125 later, and separately says about 50% down; the 211 to 123-125 move is closer to 40%, and the 211 peak differs from the 225.64 intraday high.

c23.note: Yahoo shows an intraday market cap of 1.933T on 11/11/2026, essentially the claimed 1.935T.

c24.note: X Corp. has been a subsidiary of xAI since March 28, 2025, and xAI has been a SpaceX subsidiary since February 2, 2026.

c25.note: X is a wholly owned subsidiary with no separate market price, and no standalone valuation appears in the sources, though absence of a figure cannot be proven.

c26.note: The March 2025 xAI deal valued X at $33B ($45B enterprise value less $12B debt), the latest disclosed figure in the sources.

c27.note: It was an all-stock deal between Musk-controlled companies, so the price was set internally rather than by the market.

c28.note: Bloomberg on Feb 4, 2026 said XAI Holdings owns the AI startup and X and is saddled with billions in debt.

c29.note: The LinkedIn post gives the $116B figure from 29% of 20% of $2T (0.29 × 0.2 × 2,000 = 116); it is a simplified personal estimate, not company-confirmed.

c30.note: The post states 3.5x from 2022 and 9.3x from the 2024 low.

c32.note: X is a subsidiary of xAI, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX, so combined-entity valuations cannot be attributed to X alone; this is a reasonable caveat supported by the ownership structure.

c34.note: The cited SpaceX IPO and merger material comes from Wikipedia pages, and none of the passages are from SpaceX SEC filings, so this is a sourcing caveat that holds.

c31.note: Multiple outlets report SpaceX's Super Intelligence segment had Q3 2026 revenue of $7.56B, per the Oct 20, 2026 results.
